//: Mercury · LIQUID METAL ON TRUE BLACK: purely black and white, with chrome
//1: highlights. THE source for every shell surface (quickshell/: bar, launcher,
//2: OSD, power menu). No upstream palette — every role is a grey lifted from the
//3: wallpaper, a render of a liquid-metal figure, head and shoulders, on pure
//4: black with faint white specks: the black, the metal's shadow side, its mid
//5: tone, the specular whites. `tokens` names each role after what it is there
//6: so the mapping stays traceable. theme.lua still owns WINDOW chrome (gaps,
//7: border, blur, shadow); CI cross-checks it.
//8: No-hue rule, the dark half of manga's: no hue anywhere, not even for state.
//9: Every role is a grey, and state is told by WEIGHT, not hue — mirrored for a
//10: dark ground, so the ramp runs BRIGHTER as it gets worse, like metal heating
//11: white: CHROME (#dedede, the specular edge) is the frame — island rims, window
//12: border, lock ring — brushed SILVER one weight under it is every readout, the
//13: metal's lit mid tone is the launcher, pending (`warn`) is brighter than the
//14: readout and fine (`ok`) quieter, and `urgent` is pure white, the only thing
//15: brighter than the frame. A pending count reads as a brighter figure, a low
//16: battery as the whitest thing on the bar, and the alert is the pulse Chip.qml
//17: draws, not a color. readoutBright is the highlight, pure white too: the
//18: active workspace is an emissive white lozenge with the digit in `ground`
//19: (modules/Workspaces.qml) — the one specular point on the bar. The lozenge
//20: and the alert share a hex on purpose; what tells them apart is the pulse.
//21: The ground is TRUE BLACK: the panel is an OLED, and a black pixel is off —
//22: the metal's shadow side (#101010) is the first lit surface above it.
name: mercury
//tokens: What in the picture -> role, so a palette bump stays traceable. Sampled: the ground is #000000, the metal's shadow side #0d0d0d, its mid tone #5a5a5a, the highlights up to #ffffff. The quiet greys (tarnish, pewter) and the state greys are the shadow and the highlight stepped by weight. warn/ok/urgent are weights, not scenery: pending is a step brighter than the silver, fine a step under the mid tone, urgent is the highlight itself — white-hot.
//contrast: Measured (WCAG, sRGB blend) on the three surfaces that carry type: `surface`; the bar island — `#000000` at 0.70 over the top strip, which is pure black (#000000 measured, p99 = 1; composite #000000); the launcher window — `ground` at 0.80 over the picture's centre (#262626, the figure's head → #080808). dim 3.5 / 3.9 / 3.7, dormant 5.7 / 6.2 / 6.0, frame 14.1 / 15.6 / 14.9, readout 9.2 / 10.1 / 9.7, readoutBright 19.0 / 21.0 / 20.0, launcher 6.8 / 7.5 / 7.1, warn 11.4 / 12.6 / 12.0, ok 4.7 / 5.2 / 4.9, urgent 19.0 / 21.0 / 20.0, text 16.1 / 17.8 / 17.0. `ground` on `readoutBright` (the lozenge's digit) 21.0:1; `ground` on `frame` 15.6:1; the launcher's selected row (launcher on its own 18% tint, #222222) 5.7:1; `ground` on `launcher` (the terminal's selection, GTK's accent print) 7.5:1.
//quiet: `dim` is the tarnish: the brief's #6a6a6a already clears 3:1 on `surface` (3.5:1), so it is not printed up — on true black the quiet greys read brighter than they would on any other dark ground, and the risk runs the other way (a quiet grey that looks like a readout). The state greys are kept apart by at least a weight: readout 9.2 → warn 11.4 → urgent 19.0 on `surface`, and `ok` (4.7:1) sits a step under the launcher so a charging percentage reads as cooler metal, never as a readout.
//effects: Polished metal, not neon: no text glow. The panel texture is chrome — a white sheen on the top half of every panel fading to nothing just above the middle, a hard horizon, shadow deepening on the bottom half (components/Texture.qml `chrome`): the classic chrome split, the bar lit from above. 0.2 over the kind's resting 0.16: the fill is black glass over black, and the sheen has to read as light on metal, not a grey tint.
//bar: Bar identity. Black glass on black: islands in `ground` (#000000) at 0.70 — the strip the bar covers is pure black, so the fill can be well under opaque and what shows through the blur is the specks — with a 1px CHROME rim at 50% (the specular edge, the one lit line on each island), 10px corners (the one radius), no accent line, and a WHITE bloom (0.14 over 16px): the bloom is drawn in `frame`, which is near-white — a chrome edge catching light, the one bloom the theme allows. The composite is #000000: `dim` 3.9:1, `dormant` 6.2:1, `readout` 10.1:1, `text` 17.8:1.
//launcher: Launcher identity: a 1px frame in the metal's lit mid tone (`launcher`, the one surface that covers the bar gets the one weight the bar never uses) around black glass at 0.8, 10px window (the one corner), 7px input + rows (the chips' corner). The selected row is the mid tone on its own 18% tint: 5.7:1.
//osd: OSD identity: a full pill — a drop of mercury — with a 1px chrome frame and a white track (the readout, brushed silver), 0.8 so the black still shows under it.
//session: Power-menu identity: 10px tiles (the one corner) with a 1px chrome edge at 50% (the islands' rim), over a 0.8 black scrim — the figure goes to the dark behind the menu, and on an OLED most of the screen simply goes off.
//wallpaper: Shared by hyprlock.conf (brightness) and sddm/Main.qml (1 - brightness scrim). 0.7, above the night themes' resting 0.55: black does not need dimming — a black pixel at any brightness is still off — and what dims is the figure's highlights, a little, so the lock reads as the metal under lower light rather than a greyed photo. The stack sits over pure black either way (hyprlock.conf, LAYOUT NOTE).
